transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
I came in because my eating has gotten all mixed up for months. Some days I barely eat—just toast and coffee—and other days I’ll be in the bakery buying sweets I don’t even really enjoy.
When this happens, do you ever eat an unusually large amount of food in a short period of time?
I’m not really sure what counts as unusually large. I do buy sweets sometimes, but I don’t think I eat a huge amount all at once.
After eating, do you ever make yourself vomit to try to prevent weight gain?
No, I haven’t made myself vomit after eating.
Are you very afraid of gaining weight?
I’m not sure I’d say I’m very afraid of it. It’s not something I think about a lot.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most days?
Yeah, most days. I wake up with this heavy, sad feeling, and even when I’m in my kitchen making coffee, it feels like all the warmth has gone out of things.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?
Yeah. I used to get excited about quilting squares, bowling night, planning potlucks—but now I look at my supplies or the church calendar and I just can’t make myself care like I used to.
Have you noticed your appetite has decreased?
It’s been all over the place for months. Some days I barely eat—just pick at toast and coffee—but other days I’ll buy a bunch of sweets, even though I don’t really enjoy them.
When you buy those sweets, do you feel unable to stop eating once you start?
I’m not sure I’d say I can’t stop. I’ll eat some, but it’s more that I buy them without really thinking, then they’re just there.
Have you been feeling worthless?
Yes. Even when people at church tell me I’m doing fine, I can’t shake the feeling everybody in Manawa knows I’m letting my aunt down. Like they’re whispering about what a burden I’ve become.
Have you been having thoughts that life isn’t worth living, or thoughts of hurting yourself?
I’m not sure what you mean exactly. I’ve been feeling pretty low, but I haven’t really thought about hurting myself.
Do you believe people in town are actually talking about you and saying you’re a burden?
Yes... I do. It feels like people in Manawa know I’ve let my aunt down, and they’re whispering about me being a burden.
Are you certain that people in town are whispering about you being a burden?
Yes. I mean, people at church say I’m doing fine, but I still feel sure they know I’m letting my aunt down. It seems like everybody in Manawa is whispering about what a burden I’ve become.

Eating-disorder features were not supported because there was no clear binge eating, no compensatory behaviors, and no prominent fear of weight gain.
